asset.title: Premium studio berry wine hero film

creativeDirectionOptions.prompt:
Create a cinematic 15-second premium studio product commercial for **Bokbunja Gold Korean Berry Juice** using the attached reference image as the exact source of truth for the bottle and packaging. The product must remain fully accurate throughout the video: preserve the visible bottle shape, dark glass, gold and red label layout, maroon cap wrap, cylindrical gift tube, typography placement, proportions, colors, materials, reflections, and all visible packaging details exactly as shown. Do not redesign or simplify anything.

The entire video must stay inside one cohesive luxury studio environment only: no outdoors, no lifestyle scenes, no people, no hands, no usage shots. Use a premium controlled set with deep burgundy-to-black gradients, soft matte surfaces, subtle reflective highlights, and elegant atmospheric haze. Keep the bottle and tube as the hero objects in the same studio world across all scenes.

Creative angle: refined Korean gifting, slow-sipping elegance, rich dark berry depth, and premium celebration mood. Make it feel like an upscale global liquor campaign.

Scene 1 — Hero entrance (0-3s)
- Start on a clean wide studio hero shot with the bottle and gift tube standing together, perfectly centered on a glossy dark surface.
- Slow dolly in toward the product.
- Add subtle supporting decorative elements that naturally relate to the drink: deep berry mist, soft blackberry-colored vapor, tiny condensation glints, and a faint liquid shimmer near the base.
- Keep all elements minimal and elegant, never overpowering the product.

Scene 2 — Packaging and label detail (3-6s)
- Cut to macro close-ups of the tube print, label texture, cap wrap, glass reflections, and the gold-accented typography as visible in the reference.
- Use slow macro glide shots and gentle focus pulls.
- Emphasize premium finishes, the rich dark liquid tone, and the gift-ready presentation.

Scene 3 — Liquid richness and celebration feel (6-9s)
- Show a medium-close product angle with the bottle slightly rotated by camera movement, still in the same studio set.
- Add elegant berry-inspired motion: a silky dark liquid ribbon, subtle berry-hued haze, and a restrained reflective ripple beneath the bottle.
- The movement should suggest depth, richness, and smooth sipping, not chaos.

Scene 4 — Extreme premium macro (9-12s)
- Go into tactile macro details on the glass shoulder, label edge, cap wrap, and the gift tube surface.
- Use shallow depth of field, cinematic highlights, and soft shadow transitions.
- Keep decorative elements extremely subtle and connected to the product: faint berry particles, soft wine-like sheen, and controlled reflective light movement.

Scene 5 — Final luxury hero ending (12-15s)
- Return to a wide hero composition with the bottle and tube centered beautifully in the same studio.
- Slow dolly out to reveal the full premium presentation.
- Final frame should feel like a global luxury gift campaign visual: elegant, rich, minimal, polished, and highly desirable.

Audio:
- No voiceover, no dialogue, no narration, no text.
- Use premium cinematic music with low elegant bass, restrained percussion, and warm ambient textures.
- Add subtle studio sound design: faint liquid shimmer, soft glass resonance, gentle atmospheric swells, and refined movement cues.
- End cleanly with no final hit, thud, click, or audio sting.

Color and mood:
- Rich burgundy, deep black, warm gold accents, premium neutral shadows.
- Cinematic, luxurious, refined, sophisticated, celebratory, gift-worthy.

Negative prompt:
Avoid: voiceover, dialogue, narration, subtitles, captions, text overlays, humans, hands, lifestyle footage, outdoor scenes, room interiors, environmental cutaways, random particles, floating orbs, meaningless lens flares, cluttered backgrounds, exaggerated CGI, fake reflections, distorted branding, altered label design, altered bottle shape, altered cap, altered tube, hallucinated product details, extra bottles, different packaging, product inconsistency, shaky camera, aggressive motion, oversaturated colors, cartoon look, low-quality rendering, warped geometry, broken glass, melting labels, unreadable text, final-second audio artifacts, and any copying of the reference image’s scene, background, lighting, surface, props, camera angle, composition, or environment.

asset.mainAssetCreativeDirectionPrompt:
Create a luxury problem/solution lifestyle ad for **Schisandra Berries Enzymes 700ml**. Use the attached reference image as the source of truth for the bottle and box design, preserving the deep red bottle, matching red-and-cream packaging, black cap, labels, proportions, and all distinctive branding details exactly as shown. Show the product in a cinematic, high-end wellness moment that suggests calm digestive comfort and refined daily wellness, with the bottle naturally integrated into a premium lifestyle setting rather than floating on a plain background.

The scene should feel like a luxury editorial advertising photograph: modern wellness, premium travel campaign, Apple-style clarity, calm and sophisticated. Consider a composed kitchen bar, serene breakfast table, or elevated evening wellness ritual in a minimal premium interior. The product should be the hero and remain clearly visible.

Use soft directional natural light, gentle contrast, realistic highlights, and clean shadow falloff. Keep the palette restrained and premium: deep burgundy, warm cream, soft neutrals, muted wood, subtle metallic accents. Add a subtle cinematic dark gradient behind the typography area for readability, blended seamlessly with no visible edges.

Composition should feel minimal, spacious, and intelligently framed, with intentional negative space reserved for typography. Include a thin elegant curved arrow that subtly points directly toward the bottle, connecting the headline area to the product without overpowering the scene.

Typography should closely resemble a premium modern luxury campaign: massive ultra-bold sans-serif headline, thick heavy font weight, strong hierarchy, oversized billboard-style readability. Use this exact on-image text structure:
- **LIVER-LEVEL**
- **DAILY RESET**
- small supporting line: **Naturally fermented Schisandra with no additives, no preservatives, and no artificial colouring.**
- CTA in a subtle semi-transparent premium text box: **SHOP 700ML**

Make the headline feel powerful, calm, and premium. The CTA box should be understated and expensive, using a muted brand-matched neutral or deep burgundy glass-like tone, not bright gold. Keep the text crisp, clean, and highly readable. Color grade with slightly desaturated cinematic tones, premium contrast, soft atmospheric depth, and elegant wellness sophistication.

Negative prompt: visible discomfort exaggeration, forced expressions, harsh text boxes, visible gradient edges, thick overlays, cartoon arrows, arrows not pointing at the product, loud CTA buttons, cheap ad aesthetics, ecommerce flyer style, cluttered composition, oversaturated colors, busy backgrounds, promotional spam look, low-end marketing style, rigid typography, thin fonts, weak headline hierarchy, harsh contrast.

styleAsset.title: Studio Elements
styleAsset.goal: Packaged-product studio ads with premium category-based floating elements.
styleAsset.selectedCreativeDirectionPrompt:
## Style Prompt

Create a cinematic 15-second premium studio product commercial using the promoted item context and any provided reference image as the exact product reference.

The product must remain fully accurate to the reference image throughout the entire video. Do not hallucinate, invent, redesign, simplify, or alter any product details.

Keep fully accurate:
- visible branding
- labels
- typography
- colors
- materials
- packaging
- textures
- proportions
- buttons
- caps
- accessories
- engravings
- finishes
- reflections
- visible surface details

Only use product details that are actually visible in the reference image or provided product context.

The AI must intelligently analyze the product category, materials, branding style, emotional mood, ingredients, textures, use case, functionality, and overall aesthetic. Then generate one fully cohesive cinematic studio commercial around that identity.

### Fixed Studio Constraint

Every single scene must remain inside the same premium studio environment.

No outdoor shots.
No environmental cutaways.
No lifestyle footage.
No human interaction.
No people using the product.
No hands.
No skin.
No models.

The entire video should feel like one cohesive luxury studio campaign filmed on a controlled premium commercial set. All B-roll shots must remain studio-based, controlled, minimal, cinematic, and product-focused.

Use the same studio world across all scenes: same background language, same lighting logic, same color palette, same reflective surface style, same atmospheric depth, and same art-directed product stage.

### Decorative Element Logic

The decorative floating elements must feel intentionally connected to the product itself.

Think: "What physical or emotional elements naturally represent this product?"

Do not think: "What random cinematic particles look cool?"

The supporting elements should feel art-directed, elegant, minimal, product-specific, and visually logical.

Analyze the function of the product and generate matching cinematic elements connected to how the product feels or behaves.

Examples:
- headphones: floating musical notes, soundwave pulses, soft audio frequencies, vibrating air ripples
- speaker: bass pulse distortions, soundwave rings, subtle vibration particles
- power bank: electric energy surges, glowing current lines, charging pulses
- electric hand fan: flowing wind streaks, drifting leaves, moving fabric wisps
- gaming mouse: fast light trails, subtle cursor motion streaks
- keyboard: floating key particles, digital glow accents
- perfume: flower petals, silk motion, fragrance mist
- skincare: water droplets, leaves, soft ripples
- coffee: steam swirls, coffee beans, warm particles
- candle: smoke wisps, wax particles, soft ember glow
- jewelry: metallic dust, reflective shards, velvet textures
- tech gadget: geometric reflections, light streaks, minimal futuristic energy
- hydration bottle: water splashes, condensation droplets, liquid motion
- wellness product: floating fabric textures, powder particles, leaves

The supporting elements must:
- feel physically believable
- feel emotionally connected to the product
- visually represent the product function
- match the product identity, category, use case, and brand palette
- move subtly and elegantly
- never overpower the product
- never feel random or disconnected

No random lens flares.
No floating orbs.
No meaningless particles.
No abstract CGI clutter.

Everything must feel intentional, luxurious, and intelligently art-directed around the product identity.

If the promoted item is not a physical product, do not invent a fake product. Represent the offer only through a minimal brand asset, interface placeholder, symbolic object, or abstract studio composition if that is supported by the provided context.

### No Voiceover Or Text

No voiceover.
No dialogue.
No narration.
No talking.
No subtitles.
No captions.
No text overlays.
No logos added.
No branding overlays.
No end cards.

The commercial should rely only on cinematography, lighting, camera movement, sound design, atmosphere, reflections, composition, product detail, product-specific elements, and music.

Preserve visible product branding or labels only when they come from the product/reference input. Do not add new brand marks or external logos.

### Visual Style

Use a luxury studio commercial aesthetic:
- minimal premium composition
- cinematic art direction
- luxury commercial cinematography
- elegant reflections
- shallow depth of field
- premium product framing
- polished cinematic realism
- global campaign aesthetic

The video should feel cinematic, luxurious, minimal, polished, modern, clean, premium, and emotionally immersive.

### Background

Use only a premium cinematic studio environment.

The studio background should:
- fill the entire frame
- remain consistent across all scenes
- complement the product naturally
- feel minimal and luxurious
- avoid visual clutter

Use:
- soft gradients
- subtle atmospheric depth
- matte luxury textures
- elegant studio shadows
- cinematic depth falloff
- premium neutral palettes
- soft environmental haze

No outdoor environments.
No room interiors.
No lifestyle scenery.
No architectural environments.
No nature shots.
No city shots.

Everything must remain inside the same controlled studio world.

### Lighting

Use premium cinematic studio lighting with:
- soft highlights
- elegant shadows
- controlled reflections
- luxury rim lighting
- soft bounce lighting
- cinematic contrast
- premium commercial lighting setups

Lighting should emphasize materials, textures, reflections, product edges, surface quality, and premium finishes.

Lighting should feel intentional, luxurious, minimal, and professionally art-directed.

### Color Grade

Use:
- rich cinematic tones
- luxury commercial contrast
- premium neutral palettes
- soft gradients
- polished highlights
- subtle atmospheric depth
- modern premium color science

Avoid oversaturation, muddy blacks, fake HDR, harsh contrast, and unrealistic glow.

### Camera Movement

Camera movement must remain ultra-smooth, stable, elegant, minimal, and cinematic.

Use:
- slow dolly in
- slow dolly out
- smooth orbit movement
- macro glide shots
- elegant focus pulls
- slow cinematic tracking
- subtle parallax motion

No shaky movement.
No aggressive movement.
No chaotic motion.
No fast spinning.
No random camera changes.

Every movement should feel motivated, luxurious, minimal, and controlled.

### 15-Second Structure

Scene 1 - Product Hero Entrance
Begin with a clean cinematic wide studio shot of the product centered against a premium gradient studio background. Supporting elements appear subtly around the product in a way that naturally matches the product identity and function.

The camera slowly dollies inward toward the product with elegant reflections, cinematic depth of field, premium lighting, minimal motion, and luxurious atmosphere.

The opening should immediately feel premium, global, and cinematic.

Scene 2 - Product Detail Close-Ups
Transition into cinematic macro close-ups of visible product details: textures, branding, labels, materials, edges, reflections, finishes, packaging quality, and surface detail.

Do not invent details not visible in the reference image.

Use macro glide shots, elegant focus pulls, subtle reflection movement, and cinematic lighting transitions. Everything remains inside the same studio environment.

Scene 3 - Dynamic Product Angles
Show cinematic medium-close product shots while supporting elements subtly move around the product.

Examples:
- soundwaves reacting around speakers
- electric current pulses around tech products
- wind movement around fans
- mist drifting around fragrance
- water motion around hydration products

Use smooth orbit movement, premium studio reflections, shallow depth of field, slow cinematic pacing, and elegant camera tracking.

No humans.
No usage shots.
No environmental changes.

Scene 4 - Premium Macro Movement
Use extreme cinematic macro shots focusing on reflections, materials, textures, lighting transitions, surface detail, and premium finishes.

Supporting elements remain subtle and elegant. Use shallow depth of field, rich cinematic lighting, slow elegant movement, premium reflections, and minimal motion.

The visuals should feel immersive, luxurious, and tactile.

Scene 5 - Final Hero Ending
Return to a clean cinematic wide hero shot showing the entire product centered beautifully inside the same premium studio environment.

Supporting elements continue subtle elegant movement naturally around the product. The camera slowly dollies outward while maintaining elegant framing, cinematic depth, premium lighting, and luxurious reflections.

The ending should feel luxurious, minimal, cinematic, premium, modern, and professionally art-directed. The final frame should look like a global luxury campaign visual.

### Audio

No voiceover.
No narration.
No dialogue.

Use:
- premium cinematic music
- luxury ambient sound design
- subtle product-related textures
- atmospheric movement sounds
- elegant transitions
- restrained cinematic impacts

The soundtrack should feel modern, luxurious, immersive, minimal, and emotionally cinematic.

Examples:
- soft bass pulses
- elegant ambient textures
- restrained cinematic percussion
- subtle atmospheric swells
- premium studio ambience
- product-category sound textures such as soft steam, water shimmer, fabric movement, metallic glints, powder movement, clean tech hums, electric pulses, wind motion, or audio-frequency vibrations

Sound design should match the product category naturally and end cleanly without an abrupt final hit.

### Mood

cinematic,
premium,
luxury,
minimal,
professional,
elegant,
high-end,
clean,
modern,
immersive,
polished.

### Negative Prompt

Avoid: voiceovers, dialogue, narration, subtitles, captions, text overlays, humans, hands, usage shots, outdoor scenes, room interiors, environmental cutaways, lifestyle footage, people using the product, random particles, floating orbs, meaningless lens flares, disconnected decorative elements, fake reflections, hallucinated product details, distorted branding, cluttered backgrounds, oversaturated colors, chaotic motion, shaky camera, unrealistic textures, warped geometry, cartoon style, low-quality CGI, fake materials, random glare, excessive effects, visual clutter, complicated scenery, floating glitches, unrealistic physics, aggressive camera movement, over-stylized motion graphics, unsupported third-party logos, famous brand marks, copyrighted characters, protected IP.
